sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Engineering practices questions test how a candidate collaborates, makes architectural decisions, and manages technical debt — the non-coding skills that determine whether a mid-level engineer grows into a senior one. Code review at Rails shops follows the same principle as anywhere: anchor on intent first (is this solving the right problem?), architecture second (is the abstraction right?), style last (RuboCop handles this). ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) are the structured format for capturing why a decision was made — context, decision, consequences — especially valuable in Rails codebases where a choice between service objects and concerns made three years ago has compounding effects. Technical debt in Rails typically accumulates in fat models, skipped database indexes, and test suites that use create when build_stubbed would do.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: code-review, adr-technical-debt, technical-leadership. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
